title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of §XII 'Rétrospective', a summary of the group schemes over Z that Grothendieck built while studying the 'équation des lacets' in the modular case.

Data. G = GL(2)_Z. The two elements are ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 6) and σ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] (order 4). They generate SL2(Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6.

Tori.
- T_ρ = {cρ+d : det(cρ+d) = c²+cd+d² invertible} is the centralizer of ρ in GL2. It is the Weil restriction Res_{Z[ζ_3]/Z} G_m, a norm-type torus over Z.
- T_σ = {tσ+u : t²+u² invertible} ≅ Res_{Z[i]/Z} G_m is the centralizer of σ.

Normalizer piece. N'_σ = {b ∈ G : bσb^{-1} = εσ, ε² = 1} is the stabilizer of σ up to sign. It sits in the exact sequence 1 → T_σ → N'_σ → μ_2 → 1 via δ_σ. Since -σ = σ^{-1}, this is the normalizer of T_σ: a non-split torus extended by the Weyl element.

The group scheme M_{ρ,σ}. It is the closed subgroup scheme of G × T_ρ × N'_σ of triples x = (U, a, b) with
- χ(x) := det U = det b, and
- det b = ε'·det a, with ε'² = 1.
The sign ε' is called ε_3(x) and lives in μ_2.

The group scheme SM_{ρ,σ}. It adds a fourth component u ∈ B'_0 = {[[μ,λ],[0,1]]}, the affine group G_a ⋊ G_m, subject to det u = det U. So SM = B'_0 ×_{G_m} M, the fiber product over det and χ.

Structure.
- L_0 = G_a = {[[1,λ],[0,1]]} is the kernel of SM → M, so M ≅ SM/L_0.
- The map x ↦ (U, a, b, i_{T_0}(χ(x))), with i_{T_0}(μ) = diag(μ,1), splits this surjection. Hence SM ≅ M ⋉ L_0 (semidirect product).

Role. These are presumably the symmetry or 'Galois-type' groups acting on the scheme of solutions of the loop equation. The next page continues by embedding M via (Θ_G, Θ_ρ, Θ_σ, χ, ε_2, ε_3) and introduces SΣ*_{ρ,σ}, defined by the equation αρ(α)^{-1} = ε·βσ(β)^{-1}·ε_1(μ-1).

All the statements on this page are routine group-scheme bookkeeping. They are consistent: a fiber product of B'_0 = G_a ⋊ G_m with M over G_m splits as stated.
errors: Formula (1) is internally inconsistent with (3). (1) lists four factors (G × T_ρ × N'_σ × G), with one G struck out, while x = (U, a, b) has three components. Read correctly, M ⊂ GL(2) × T_ρ × N'_σ; the ordering on the page is muddled by the corrections.

Over Z, ε² = 1 defines μ_2, which is non-reduced at 2, and σ ≡ -σ mod 2. The fppf-surjectivity of δ_σ: N'_σ → μ_2 in (11) at the prime 2 is not justified on the page and deserves checking. It is clear over Z[1/2].

Writing T_ρ as the centralizer of ρ and N'_σ as an extension requires that centralizers of regular elliptic elements be smooth tori over Z. This holds, but only because Z[ρ] ≅ Z[ζ_3] and Z[σ] ≅ Z[i] are étale away from 3 and 2 resp., and are Weil restrictions over all of Z. This is not commented on.

ideas.what: Centralizers of the elliptic generators ρ, σ of SL2(Z) as Weil-restriction tori over Z: Res_{Z[ζ3]/Z}G_m and Res_{Z[i]/Z}G_m
ideas.modern_name: Non-split (CM) tori / centralizers of regular semisimple elements in GL2
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 treats tori and centralizers in general

ideas.what: N'_σ, the normalizer of the torus T_σ as an extension of μ2 by T_σ
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of a maximal torus / Weyl group extension
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general theory of normalizers of tori)

ideas.what: Group schemes M_{ρ,σ} and SM_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 ×_{G_m} M_{ρ,σ} = M ⋉ G_a, encoding the symmetries of the modular loop equation
ideas.modern_name: Symmetry group scheme of the solution scheme of a 'loop equation' for SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; part of Grothendieck's unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the symmetries of the 'équation des lacets' in the modular case (ρ of order 6, σ of order 4) as explicit affine group schemes over Z, built from the CM tori of Z[ζ3] and Z[i], a torus normalizer, and the affine group. This is an arithmetic-geometric encoding of the conjugacy data of SL2(Z)'s elliptic elements. The broader programme does not appear to have been developed in the literature, although the content of this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: Par bien des détours inutilement compliqués, j'ai fini de façon bien simple par construire deux schémas en groupes sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may offer a scheme-theoretic framework for studying solutions of loop/braid-type equations over Z (e.g. related to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations in the genus-0 modular case). Its value depends on the surrounding pages, not this summary page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a retrospective summary of fairly routine group-scheme constructions (tori, normalizer, fiber product, semidirect product). Its interest lies only in being part of an unpublished programme on the loop equation; nothing here is surprising on its own.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top likely reads '542' (consistent with the 293–650 pagination of the cote), not '842'.
In (1) the first factor G is struck out, with 'GL(2)_Z' written below as the meaning of G. In (2) the last factor (a G/B symbol) is struck out.
The line after (4) should read 'donc SM_{ρ,σ} = B'_0 ×_{G_m} M_{ρ,σ}', with G_m written as a subscript under the ×.
In (7) the last component is i_{T_0}(μ) (the struck-out text is a correction), 'où μ = χ(x)'.
